cases.text: The first effect held, t(58) = 2.36, p = .022; the second did not, t(58) = 2.36, p = .25; the third was off by a hair, t(21) = 2.15, p = .048.

Participants in the treatment group (M = 4.2, SD = 1.1) scored higher than controls (M = 3.5, SD = 1.3), t(58) = 2.36, p = .022, d = 0.61. A one-way ANOVA on the three conditions was significant, F(2, 57) = 4.52, p = .015, and condition was unrelated to gender, χ²(2, N = 60) = 5.99, p = .050. Ranks differed across the groups, H(2) = 9.57, p = .008; scores were correlated, r(58) = .31, p = .016, and a Wilcoxon test gave z = −3.17, p = .002.
